title: Ops Conductor CLI: typed runbook iterations with safe replay and parameterized dry-run
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight CLI (ops-conductor) that converts curated runbooks into typed, parameterized tasks which can be executed with strong safety modes: dry-run, simulated replay, and guarded production execution. The goal is to make runbooks first-class developer artifacts (schemas, validation, idempotency hints), integrate telemetry and audit logs, and provide a fast feedback loop for SREs and first-line support to iterate on procedures without risking production changes.
background_and_rationale: Current runbook execution is fragmented: markdown docs, ad-hoc scripts, and occasional non-typed tooling. This causes inconsistent inputs, hidden side effects, and difficult replayability for incident postmortems. The Ops Conductor CLI will standardize how runbooks are authored, validated, and executed across hosted/dedicated/private environments, and enable safe automation adoption by embedding explicit preconditions, parameter types, and revert hooks.
acceptance_criteria: CLI can ingest a runbook descriptor (YAML/JSON) and emit a typed task manifest with parameter schema
Execution modes: dry-run (no external side effects), simulate-replay (replay with mocked infra calls), and execute (with RBAC gating) are implemented
Every executed task emits structured telemetry (start/stop, params, success/failure, duration, run_id) to internal events pipeline
Idempotency tokens and optimistic checks are supported by the task runtime to prevent duplicate executions
A minimal UX for interactive prompts and non-interactive CI usage is documented and covered by e2e tests
plan: Design runbook descriptor schema and authoring guide
Prototype CLI: ingest -> validate -> simulate -> run
Integrate telemetry hooks and audit log emission
Add RBAC gating and optional approval workflow for high-risk steps
Ship beta to SRE and Support teams; collect feedback and iterate
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental production changes during replay. Mitigation: make dry-run the default and require explicit --execute flag plus approval for high-risk tasks
Risk: schema drift across teams. Mitigation: include schema validation and a linter in the CLI with CI check templates
Risk: overreliance on CLI leading to unreviewed scripts. Mitigation: require changelist and PR review for adding new runbook manifests to the central repo
